about.text: 18th Street Arts Center is a nonprofit artist residency and public-programs organization in Santa Monica, California, founded in 1988 by Susanna Bixby Dakin and Linda Frye Burnham out of a 1970s-80s community of feminist and performance artists that included Judy Chicago and Barbara T. Smith. Now one of the largest artist-residency programs in Southern California, it hosts local, national, and international artists for live/work studio stays, alongside organizations-in-residence such as Highways Performance Space. Its program blends exhibitions and public events in the Atrium Gallery and Artist's Hearth with community-engagement initiatives like Culture Mapping 90404, reflecting a long-standing commitment to socially engaged, research-driven contemporary art practice.

about.text: Anat Ebgi is a contemporary art gallery founded in 2012 by Anat Ebgi, with locations in Los Angeles on Wilshire Boulevard and in New York City's Tribeca. The gallery represents an intergenerational and international roster of emerging and established artists, and manages the estates of Tina Girouard and Gloria Klein. Its program emphasizes museum-caliber exhibitions and performances, including a historical survey marking the 50th anniversary of Womanhouse, and the global representation of eco-feminist artist Faith Wilding. Works by gallery artists are held in major American and international museum collections, including LACMA, MoMA, the Whitney, SFMOMA, and the Stedelijk Museum. The gallery participates regularly in international art fairs such as Art Basel, Frieze, The Armory Show, and The Art Show, and joined the Art Dealers Association of America in 2023.

about.text: Founded in 1989, Armory Center for the Arts is a nonprofit visual arts organization based in a historic 1932 California National Guard Armory building in Old Pasadena. It operates as a hybrid museum and art school, presenting contemporary art exhibitions alongside artist-led education programs for children, teens, and adults. Its roots trace back to the Pasadena Art Institute's Junior Museum program (1922), later evolving through the Pasadena Art Museum's Children's Art Workshop and the Pasadena Art Workshops before becoming the Armory in 1989. The organization emphasizes socially engaged, often BIPOC-centered contemporary art and free community-based art education, serving over 18,000 people annually across Pasadena and Los Angeles County, with particular focus on under-resourced neighborhoods and system-impacted communities.

about.text: The Box is a Los Angeles gallery founded in 2007 by Mara McCarthy, in conversation with her father, the artist Paul McCarthy. It first opened on Chung King Road in Chinatown before relocating in 2012 to the Arts District of Downtown Los Angeles. The gallery built its program around historically overlooked and forgotten artists, particularly those working in performance, feminist, and radical political practices, including figures such as Barbara T. Smith, Simone Forti, Stan VanDerBeek, and Wally Hedrick. Over time the program expanded to include dance, painting, music and sound, sculpture, social justice projects, performance, and gallery editions, positioning itself as an artist-centered space engaging the commercial art market on its own terms. The Box announced its closing in April 2026 after nineteen years of operation.

about.text: Brand Library & Art Center occupies the restored 1904 Miradero mansion, the former Glendale estate of civic figure Leslie C. Brand, whose Indo-Islamic-styled house was donated to the city upon his death in 1925 and converted into a public library that opened in 1956. A 1969 addition added a gallery and recital hall, and the whole complex was renovated and reopened in 2014. Operated as a branch of the City of Glendale Library, Arts & Culture Department, it combines a specialized visual-arts and music library collection with rotating exhibitions, concerts, dance performances, lectures and community arts programs, serving as a cultural and historic landmark at the base of the Verdugo Mountains.

about.text: The Broad is a contemporary art museum on Grand Avenue in downtown Los Angeles, founded in 2015 by philanthropists Eli and Edythe Broad as a gift to the city. Designed by Diller Scofidio + Renfro with Gensler, its 120,000-square-foot 'veil-and-vault' building offers free general admission and houses over 2,000 postwar and contemporary works by nearly 200 artists, including Basquiat, Warhol, Koons, Kusama, Ruscha, and Kruger. The museum is also headquarters to the Broad Art Foundation's worldwide lending library, active since 1984. Under founding director Joanne Heyler, its program emphasizes rotating temporary exhibitions, monographic surveys, and public programming often centered on social justice themes, drawing over 900,000 visitors annually.

about.text: Currency Exchange (CXLA) is a Los Angeles gallery and community arts space that pairs its exhibition schedule with social-practice programming. Rather than functioning as a conventional white-box gallery, it uses its ground-floor space—situated within affordable housing along the West Washington corridor in Mid-City—as a gathering point for artists, residents, and neighbors. Alongside rotating exhibitions, CXLA runs Community Feeds tied to each show's closing, karaoke nights during exhibitions, artist talks, workshops, and a Beauty Salon series developed with Transformation Arts and the Agape Artist Residency. It also produces a neighborhood zine documenting Mid-City businesses and stories, and invites residents to create collaborative lobby artworks. The organization frames its programming as an investment in the surrounding community's social fabric.

about.text: Dataland is an immersive media-art venue in Downtown Los Angeles, created by Refik Anadol Studio, the practice founded in 2014 by artist Refik Anadol and artist-entrepreneur Efsun Erkılıç. about.text: Diversions Fine Arts is a membership gallery in Manhattan Beach, California, founded by arts writer and curator Genie Davis. about.text: Fahey/Klein Gallery is a Los Angeles photography gallery founded in 1986 by David Fahey and Randee Klein Devlin. Ken Devlin joined as co-owner in 1998; David Fahey has led the gallery since 2016. Located on North La Brea Avenue, the gallery specializes in 20th-century and contemporary fine art photography, with an inventory of more than 8,000 prints spanning portraiture, nudes, landscapes, still life, reportage and documentary work. Its exhibition program has featured photographers from Edward Weston and Man Ray to Herb Ritts and James Nachtwey, and the gallery mounts new two-person shows roughly every five weeks. Staff also curate touring exhibitions for museums and galleries abroad, contribute to photography publications, and maintain an active secondary-market and private-collection advisory practice.

about.text: Feia is a Los Angeles gallery founded by husband-duo Thomas Martinez Pilnik and Jake Cavallo. The name, Portuguese for "ugly," reflects a program built around curiosity, humor, and unconventional beauty rather than conventional polish. Pilnik, an artist and educator, and Cavallo, a designer with an architecture background, run Feia as a hybrid of exhibitions, events, dinners, and workshops emphasizing community and food alongside visual art. The gallery represents a small roster of emerging painters, sculptors, and mixed-media artists exploring queer identity, memory, and domestic space, and is especially active on the art fair circuit across Los Angeles, New York, Miami, and Chicago. It has also built a new gallery space in the Highland Park neighborhood of Los Angeles.

about.text: Fernberger is a Los Angeles gallery founded by Emma Fernberger in January 2024. Located on North Western Avenue, it presents an intergenerational program of artists with a global outlook, placing particular emphasis on women-identifying practitioners. The program is unified by a sense of intensity and immediacy, favoring work that produces an instant visceral reaction while remaining thoughtful and historically grounded. Fernberger has described an interest in art's transformative and unifying potential, seeking pieces that are high-impact yet cerebral. The gallery has participated in major art fairs and been the subject of coverage in international publications, reflecting a growing profile within the Los Angeles gallery scene, particularly around the Melrose Hill area.

about.text: Brodin is the shared studio of Los Angeles and UK–based sculptors Gavin and Kelley Brodin, a collaborative artist duo rather than a commercial gallery representing other artists. about.text: FOYER-LA is an artist-run exhibition space in Los Angeles, founded in 2019 by artist Connie Walsh. Set behind a courtyard in front of Walsh's own studio, it describes itself as an in-between space for experimentation, dialogue, and collaboration. Since opening, the gallery has presented more than thirty projects, ranging from solo debuts to conceptually driven installations across sculpture, drawing, and performance. Its program has included artists such as Ellie Krakow, Michael Ashkin, Ana Maria Devis, and James Rose, alongside Walsh's own work. The space favors small-scale, provocative shows that explore themes of intimacy, transition, and the body, positioning itself as a laboratory for experimentation rather than a conventional commercial gallery.

about.text: Gagosian is a global gallery for modern and contemporary art founded by Larry Gagosian in Los Angeles in 1980. From that first space it has grown into a network of exhibition spaces across the United States, Europe, and Asia, designed by architects including Richard Meier, Jean Nouvel, and Selldorf Architects. The program pairs a roster of leading living artists working across painting, sculpture, photography, and design with museum-quality historical exhibitions of twentieth-century masters. The gallery also runs a publishing arm producing catalogues raisonnés, monographs, and the Gagosian Quarterly magazine, and has developed initiatives supporting artists' estates and legacy planning alongside talks, screenings, and studio-visit programming.

about.text: REDCAT (the Roy and Edna Disney CalArts Theater) is CalArts' downtown Los Angeles center for contemporary visual and performing arts, opened in November 2003 inside the Walt Disney Concert Hall complex designed by Frank Gehry. Initiated by Roy E. Disney as a gift from the Walt Disney Company and matched by Roy and Patty Disney, it houses a 250-seat black-box theater, a 3,000-square-foot gallery, and a lounge. Through performances, exhibitions, screenings, and literary events, REDCAT presents experimental and cutting-edge work by Los Angeles-based and international artists, extending CalArts' mission of experimentation, discovery, and civic discourse to a professional venue in the city's downtown cultural corridor.

about.text: Jeffrey Deitch is a contemporary art gallery founded by dealer, curator and writer Jeffrey Deitch, who opened its Los Angeles space in September 2018 after directing Deitch Projects in New York (1996–2010) and serving as director of MOCA Los Angeles. about.text: L.A. Louver is a contemporary art gallery in Venice, California, founded in 1975 by Peter and Elizabeth Goulds. It opened to the public on North Venice Boulevard in 1976 with a mission to place Southern California artists in an international context while bringing global artists to Los Angeles audiences. Over five decades the gallery has represented a roster of established postwar and contemporary painters and sculptors, mounting hundreds of exhibitions and building an extensive archive documenting its history and artists' records. about.text: La Luz de Jesus Gallery is a Los Angeles gallery founded in 1986 by entrepreneur and art collector Billy Shire. Housed inside the Soap Plant/Wacko complex on Hollywood Boulevard, the gallery is credited with helping foster what became known as the Lowbrow or Pop Surrealist movement in California art. Its program favors figurative, narrative painting and unconventional sculpture, with content spanning folk, outsider, religious, and sexually charged themes. The gallery states its mission is to bring underground art and counter-culture to a wider audience, and it also operates an Art Advisor Service connecting collectors, curators, and designers with contemporary artists worldwide.

about.text: LACMA is the largest art museum in the western United States, holding some 155,000 objects spanning 6,000 years of global art history. It traces its roots to the Los Angeles County Museum of History, Science, and Art (1910) and became an independent institution in 1961, opening on Wilshire Boulevard in 1965. The campus has grown through additions including the Anderson/Art of the Americas Building, the Pavilion for Japanese Art, BCAM, and the Resnick Pavilion, culminating in the 2026 opening of the Peter Zumthor-designed David Geffen Galleries. Located on Wilshire Boulevard in the Miracle Mile, LACMA presents rotating exhibitions across its global collection alongside public programs, education initiatives, and community partnerships, including a gallery at Charles White Elementary School.

about.text: Founded in 1954 within Barnsdall Art Park, the Los Angeles Municipal Art Gallery is the longest continuously running institution in Los Angeles devoted solely to exhibiting art. Operated by the city's Department of Cultural Affairs, it grew out of the city-led All City Outdoor Art Festivals and Kenneth Ross's vision for decentralized civic arts programming. The gallery focuses on artists connected to Los Angeles, with particular attention to underrepresented and emerging voices, alongside mid-career and established practitioners. Past exhibitors who later gained wider recognition include Carlos Almaraz, John Baldessari, Vija Celmins, David Hammons, Barbara Kruger, Kerry James Marshall, and Ed Ruscha. Admission and programs are free, and the gallery does not maintain a permanent collection.

about.text: Make Room is a contemporary art gallery in Hollywood, Los Angeles, founded in 2018 by collector and curator Emilia Yin. It occupies interconnected exhibition spaces with an outdoor courtyard and garden. The program centers on artists exploring cultural identity, conceptual practice and global perspectives, often ahead of institutional recognition, with a stated commitment to female artists, artists of color and voices working outside established centers. Shaped by Yin's position between Los Angeles and Asia, the gallery has introduced emerging artists and reframed established ones, including Terence Koh, Sun Woo, Andrew Sendor, Guimi You, Yeni Mao, Tuan Vu, Xin Liu and Jacopo Pagin. Works by its artists have entered major public collections including LACMA, the Hammer Museum and the Institute of Contemporary Art Miami.

about.text: Marian Goodman Gallery was established in New York in 1977 by Marian Goodman, who had earlier co-founded the art-publishing house Multiples, Inc. The gallery became known for introducing major European artists to American audiences and later expanded internationally, opening a Paris location in 1995 and, for a period from 2014 to 2022, a London space. In September 2023 the gallery inaugurated a permanent exhibition space in Los Angeles, extending a program that now anchors both U.S. coasts alongside its long-running Paris presence. The gallery represents more than fifty artists and estates across generations, with a program emphasizing rigorous, institutionally engaged practices in painting, sculpture, photography, film, and performance, and maintains close, long-term collaborations with its artists and with curators and institutions worldwide.

about.text: Mek Contemporary is a Los Angeles–based gallery presenting contemporary artists working across disciplines and geographies. The program pays particular attention to work engaging memory, migration, displacement, place, identity, and cultural inheritance, favoring artists with distinctive approaches to form, material, and image. about.text: Michael Kohn Gallery was founded in 1985 by Michael Kohn, opening first on Robertson Boulevard in West Hollywood before relocating in 2014 to its current home on North Highland Avenue in Los Angeles. about.text: MOCA, founded in 1979, is Los Angeles's leading museum dedicated to contemporary art, built around a collection of nearly 8,000 works with deep holdings in LA-based practice alongside international art. MOCA Grand Avenue, the museum's original and flagship site in downtown LA, was designed by architect Arata Isozaki in the 1980s and opened as his first completed US project, announcing MOCA as a major architectural presence on Bunker Hill. The museum also operates The Geffen Contemporary at MOCA, a renovated warehouse in Little Tokyo, and stewards Michael Heizer's land-art work Double Negative in Nevada. Programming spans monographic and thematic exhibitions, education initiatives, publishing, and new-media engagement.

about.text: Parrasch heijnen is a gallery in the Boyle Heights neighborhood of Los Angeles. Its program brings together postwar Los Angeles Light and Space and geometric abstraction, work by artists associated with the historic Brockman Gallery and the Black Arts Council, and a roster of contemporary painters and sculptors working in abstraction and assemblage. The gallery represents several artist estates, including those of Peter Alexander, Tony DeLap, Forrest Bess, Marcia Hafif and Alonzo Davis, alongside living artists such as Anne Appleby, Edith Baumann, Alteronce Gumby, Xylor Jane, Kristy Luck, Mildred Howard and Christine Howard Sandoval. The gallery participates regularly in international art fairs, including Frieze, Art Basel Miami Beach, NADA, Independent and the Dallas Art/Invitational fairs, and has organized historical group presentations such as 'Brockman Days' surveying the artists of the pioneering Black-owned Brockman Gallery.

about.text: Perrotin is an international contemporary art gallery founded in Paris in 1990 by Emmanuel Perrotin, then twenty-one years old. about.text: ROSEGALLERY is a Los Angeles-area gallery founded in 1991 by Rose Shoshana at the Bergamot Station Arts Center in Santa Monica. The program centers on modern and contemporary photography, spanning works that draw on the medium's history as well as contemporary photo-based art. Shoshana, who trained at Art Center College of Design and worked in editorial photography before opening the gallery, has built relationships with artists such as William Eggleston, Bruce Davidson, and Graciela Iturbide, and has collaborated with institutions including the Getty Museum and Tate Modern. The gallery represents a roster of established and emerging photographers and lens-based artists, and regularly presents work at international art fairs including Paris Photo and Photo London.

about.text: Royale Projects is a Los Angeles gallery founded in 2008, dedicated to the history and ongoing development of abstraction in painting and sculpture, alongside artists whose work is rooted in Conceptualism. The gallery has presented debut exhibitions of artists such as Helen Pashgian, associated with the California Light & Space movement, and the last new works by Dennis Oppenheim. It has organized site-responsive desert projects in Joshua Tree, including collaborations with Andrea Zittel and Phillip K. Smith III. Its downtown Los Angeles Arts District space opened in 2015. The gallery participated in The Getty's Pacific Standard Time: LA/LA and represents the estate of Clinton Hill, contributing to renewed critical interest in his abstract paintings from the New York School.

about.text: Sage Culture is an art gallery and multidisciplinary project space in the Arts District of Los Angeles, founded in 2017 by Nicolas Alonso and Marina Figueiredo. The gallery's concept grew out of a trip to Easter Island and centers on the relationship between people and nature, drawing on ancient and primitive forms of artistic expression. Its program represents artists whose work is deeply tied to natural materials, processes, and themes, spanning ceramics, textiles, photography, and mixed media. Works often blur boundaries between art, craft, and design, emphasizing process, material experimentation, and a meditative or ecological sensibility. The gallery operates by appointment only from its DTLA location.

about.text: Sea View is a Los Angeles gallery founded in 2022 by Sara Lee Hantman. about.text: Sean Kelly is a contemporary art gallery founded in 1991 by dealer Sean Kelly, originally opening its first public space on Mercer Street in SoHo before moving to a larger Chelsea location in 2001 and then to its current 22,000-square-foot building at 475 Tenth Avenue in 2012. The gallery is active on the international art-fair circuit and regularly collaborates with major museums worldwide.

about.text: Serious Topics is a small artist-run gallery in Inglewood, California, founded by artists Kristin Calabrese and Joshua Aster. Visits are by appointment, reflecting its low-key, artist-driven approach to running a commercial exhibition space.

about.text: Sprüth Magers is an international gallery for postwar and contemporary art, founded by Monika Sprüth in Cologne in 1983 and joined by Philomene Magers, whose own gallery merged with Sprüth's in 1998. Known for close, curatorially rigorous relationships with artists and museums, the gallery built its reputation on conceptual, photography-based and feminist-inflected practices, showing figures such as Rosemarie Trockel, Cindy Sherman, Barbara Kruger and John Baldessari from early on. In 2016 it opened its Los Angeles space on the Miracle Mile, its first US location, debuting with new works by Baldessari. The LA gallery continues the program's mix of longstanding conceptualists, mid-career figures and emerging voices across painting, sculpture, photography and installation.

about.text: Thinkspace Projects is a Los Angeles gallery in the West Adams District, founded in 2005 by Andrew Hosner and L. Croskey. Since its start the gallery has built an international reputation as a leading voice for the New Contemporary Art Movement, a lowbrow-descended, figurative and pop-culture-inflected strain of art that emerged on the West Coast in the 1990s. Thinkspace represents artists ranging from emerging to established, and has expanded beyond its own space to curate exhibitions with museums and partner galleries in cities such as Berlin, Hong Kong, London, New York, Detroit, Chicago and Honolulu. It also produces murals worldwide and works with organizations like POW! WOW! and RAD Napa. The gallery describes itself as artist-focused, family-run, and committed to bridging street-level and institutional art contexts.
hints: Thinkspace has spent two decades championing exactly this kind of pop-surrealist, illustration-adjacent painting, and Grabelsky's meticulous, faintly melancholic style is a good fit for a gallery that treats craft and narrative as virtues rather than liabilities.

The Fresh Series is Thinkspace's rolling showcase for Los Angeles-based artists, giving early-career and locally rooted creatives a rotating slot in the gallery's exhibition calendar alongside its bigger solo shows.

about.text: Vielmetter Los Angeles is a contemporary art gallery in the Arts District of downtown Los Angeles, located at 1700 S Santa Fe Avenue. It is owned and directed by Susanne Vielmetter and operates three exhibition spaces at that address. The gallery represents a multigenerational group of artists working across painting, sculpture, photography, video, and installation, including figures such as Nicole Eisenman, Arlene Shechet, Mickalene Thomas, Wangechi Mutu, Mary Kelly, and the estate of William Pope.L. Represented artists have participated in major international biennials, museum surveys, and art fairs, and have received sustained critical attention in publications including The New York Times, Artforum, The Guardian, and Artnet. The gallery's program spans several decades of contemporary practice, with a consistent focus on socially engaged, figurative, and materially inventive work by artists based in Los Angeles, New York, and internationally.

about.text: Weinstein Gallery was founded in San Francisco in 1992 by Rowland Weinstein, with a focus on non-objective and surrealist art spanning pre-war Europe through the New York School and Abstract Expressionism. It has also worked to revive attention to understudied artists such as Enrico Donati, Jimmy Ernst, Gordon Onslow Ford, Gerome Kamrowski and Kurt Seligmann through exhibitions, publications and museum loans. In Spring 2026 the gallery plans to open a project space in Los Angeles devoted to contemporary art, performance and multidisciplinary programming, extending its historical program into a dialogue with the present day.

about.text: Wönzimer is an independent gallery in Lincoln Heights, Los Angeles, founded by Swiss artist Alaïa Parhizi and American entrepreneur Aidan Nelson. Its German name, meaning "living room," reflects the founders' aim to create an intimate, home-like exhibition space rather than a conventional white-box gallery. The gallery represents thirteen artists working across painting, sculpture, and mixed media, and presents both solo shows and thematic group exhibitions that bring together established and emerging voices, including international projects. Beyond exhibitions, Wönzimer runs W.A.R.P., an artist residency program with on-site studios, and hosts artist talks, poetry readings, music, film screenings, and other cross-disciplinary programming. The space includes a hidden bookshelf leading to a lounge, continuing the gallery's living-room concept. Wönzimer has operated from earlier locations in Koreatown and downtown Los Angeles before settling in its current Lincoln Heights space.

about.text: Casa Ysasi is a studio and gallery in Los Angeles founded by brothers Iñigo and Pato Ysasi, built around a shared sense of hermandad, or brotherhood, rooted in family and craft. The space is divided between a gallery for exhibiting prints and curated work and a working studio and showroom where light-based objects and prototypes are developed. Ysasi Gallery operates as a rotating, two-month exhibition and installation platform, working with local and international artists whose practices sit between art, design, and craft, with an emphasis on process-driven, site-specific work. The studio side, Studio Ysasi, focuses on light as a medium, producing objects and installations meant to evoke presence and calm.
